item.title: [7] Superconductivity near two-dimensional Van Hove singularities: A determinant quantum Monte Carlo study
item.description:
Last authors: Edwin Huang, Ilya Esterlis

Authors: Gustav Romare, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko, Edwin Huang, Ilya Esterlis

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Van Hove singularities are central to the physics of kagome metals like AV3Sb5.

Tags: #superconduct #theory #kagome-adjacent

Abstract: Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the authors compute here the superconducting transition temperature T c of the two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model near ordinary and higher-order Van Hove singularities. Contrary to conventional wisdom, the authors find that the maximal T c in the model occurs away from the Van Hove singularities, when the system is in the intermediate coupling regime.

Abstract: Here, the authors show how strain allows control of the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in WSe 2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. They demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. Abstract: The p - n junction is at the heart of the first great technological revolution. Here, the authors fabricate and characterize such a junction made entirely out of cuprates superconductors thin films. They observe a charge transfer between n -type Pr 1 . 85 Ce 0 . 15 CuO 4 and p -type La 1 . 85 Sr 0 . 15 CuO 4 , from which a Mott insulating layer emerges at the atomically sharp interface. They first assess the quality of the structure through x-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy and then they explore the nature of the insulating interface arising from strong electron correlations with various electrical transport experiments.
